articles.title: What in the World - How does nine months at sea impact your mental health? - BBC Sounds
articles.summary: American sailors and marines finally had a break in Pattaya, Thailand
articles.body:
World Service , · 07 Sep 2026 , · 9 mins

After a record 250 consecutive days at sea, the USS Abraham Lincoln finally docked in Thailand last week. Half of the 5,000 crew members are under 24 years old and they’ve been on board since December, as part of the US-Israel war with Iran. There have been reports of difficult conditions on board, with food shortages, broken plumbing and concerns about the crew’s morale and mental health, but the US Navy says there haven't been severe problems on board. So how can spending months at sea impact your mental health? We speak to Dr Harold Kudler, a psychiatrist and former head of mental health policy for the U.S. Department of Veterans Affairs, about the toll this can take. We also hear from Joe Franta, a merchant mariner and YouTuber who documents his experiences working on cargo ships. He shares what it’s like to be at sea for long periods of time. Email: whatintheworld@bbc.co.uk WhatsApp: +44 330 12 33 22 6 Presenter: Hannah Gelbart Producers: William Lee Adams and Chelsea Coates Editor: Harriet Oliver

articles.title: Money Box - Numeracy Review and Petrol Prices - BBC Sounds
articles.summary: What can we expect from a major review of financial literacy?
articles.body: A new survey has suggested nearly a third of people in the UK believe they lost money last year because of their poor maths skills. One estimate puts the cost of innumeracy at £25 billion per year. To try and tackle this the government has asked a House of Lords committee to investigate. We'll hear from its chair, Lord Agnew. The price of petrol is the highest it has been for almost four years. It was autumn 2022 when petrol last topped 160p a litre. We'll look at why that is and what you can do try and bring the costs down. It's 50 years since the creation of the first index fund for ordinary investors - spearheaded by John Bogle, the founder of the American investment company The Vanguard Group. What was its impact on investing today? And, why more than £1.5 billion languishing in unclaimed, government-backed Child Trust Funds will be the focus of a new review by the Financial Conduct Authority. Presenter: Paul Lewis Reporters: Dan Whitworth and Catherine Lund Editor: Jess Quayle Senior News Editor: Sara Wadeson (First broadcast 12pm on Saturday 5th September 2026)

articles.title: Consumer Fight Back - Challenging PIP rejections at tribunal - BBC Sounds
articles.summary: Rejected for PIP? Most tribunal appeals succeed. We ask why.
articles.body:
Radio Ulster , · 05 Sep 2026 , · 56 mins

We’re talking benefits. Turned down for Personal Independence Payment? Thousands of people are challenging benefit decisions at independent tribunals, and the majority are winning. We hear why so many initial PIP assessments are being overturned and what it could mean for you. Talking openly about debt. We meet the influencer behind 'Figuring out finances at 40' who's breaking the taboo around financial struggles. From revealing exactly how much debt she's in to documenting the mistakes she's made and the practical steps she's taking to get back on track. Could your holiday booking be too good to be true? A new investigation by consumer group Which? has raised serious questions about checks on Booking.com after researchers successfully created a fake holiday rental at one of Britain's most famous addresses: 10 Downing Street. So how easy is it for fraudulent listings to slip through the net, and what should travellers look out for? articles.title: Zema estende painel em prédio na Avenida Paulista com boneco de Moraes preso  | G1
articles.standfirst: Após a ação simbólica, candidato participou de um ato do Partido Novo em frente ao Masp. O evento reuniu poucos militantes do partido.
articles.summary: Após a ação simbólica, candidato participou de um ato do Partido Novo em frente ao Masp. O evento reuniu poucos militantes do partido.
articles.body:
O candidato à Presidência da República, Romeu Zema (NOVO), realiza um ato na Avenida Paulista, em São Paulo, contra o ministro Alexandre de Moraes, na manhã desta segunda-feira (07), Dia da Independência do Brasil. — Foto: Aloisio Mauricio/Estadão Conteúdo

O ex-governador de Minas Gerais e pré-candidato à Presidência da República, Romeu Zema (Novo), estendeu na fachada de um prédio da Avenida Paulista um painel com a frase “Chega de intocáveis”.

O painel também trazia imagens de ministros do STF rindo e um boneco representando Alexandre de Moraes atrás das grades. Manifestantes do PT que estavam na avenida hostilizaram Zema e foram impedidos por policiais militares de se aproximar dele.

Sem citar Moraes, ele disse que "em qualquer país minimamente civilizado, onde se tem vergonha na cara, um ministro como esse, prestando serviços pra um bandido, teria sido expelido, teria sido expulso e, muito provavelmente, encarcerado. O lugar dele é esse. É um bandido enriquecendo porque exerce um cargo para o qual já é muito bem remunerado".

Questionado sobre a posição de Flávio Dino, Zema afirmou que o ministro integra uma “turminha” que deseja manter a situação como está porque, segundo ele, “tem muita gente poderosa se beneficiando”. O ex-governador também associou Dino aos ministros Alexandre de Moraes, Dias Toffoli e Gilmar Mendes, afirmando que eles fazem parte do mesmo grupo.

No domingo (6), Dino fez uma crítica velada à decisão do ministro Edson Fachon de encerrar o Inquérito das Fake news . Sem citar diretamente a investigação, ele disse que é a favor da conclusão das investigações. Mas questionou: "antes do prazo prescricional, um inquérito deve ser arquivado por motivo de tramitação longa? E quem decide o que é “tramitação longa”?".

Toffoli, que era relator das investigações sobre o Master no STF, se afastou do caso após revelações que mostraram que fundos ligados ao banco compraram a participação de irmãos do ministro em um resort Tayayá na cidade de Ribeirão Claro, no Paraná. Relembre o caso .

Zema tem embate antigo com o Supremo. O procurador-geral da República, Paulo Gonet, denunciou em maio o ex-governador por calúnia contra Gilmar Mendes por publicação de vídeo em que ministros são retratados como fantoches.

Zema critica Gilmar Mendes e Alexandre de Moraes — Foto: Reprodução/Redes Sociais

Após a ação simbólica, Zema participou de um ato do Partido Novo em frente ao Masp. O evento reuniu poucos militantes do partido.

Em seu discurso, Zema voltou a defender mudanças nos critérios para a escolha dos ministros do Supremo Tribunal Federal (STF). Entre as propostas apresentadas por ele está a criação de uma lista tríplice para orientar as indicações feitas pelo presidente da República.

“Eu, como presidente, não tenho nenhum receio de receber uma lista tríplice preparada pela OAB, pelo Superior Tribunal de Justiça e pelo Ministério Público Federal”, declarou.

Atualmente, os ministros do Supremo são escolhidos pelo presidente e precisam ter os nomes aprovados pela maioria absoluta do Senado. A Constituição determina que os indicados tenham entre 35 e 70 anos, notável saber jurídico e reputação considerada ilibada.

Zema afirmou que, caso seja eleito presidente, pretende escolher pessoas com mais de 60 anos e, preferencialmente, com trajetória no meio acadêmico.

“Quero alguém acima de 60 anos, de preferência que venha do mundo acadêmico. Nós precisamos de pessoas que estudaram a vida toda na área jurídica para somar no Supremo”, declarou.

O ex-governador também fez críticas aos ministros Flávio Dino, Alexandre de Moraes, Dias Toffoli e Gilmar Mendes.

Durante o pronunciamento, Zema citou ainda as investigações envolvendo Daniel Vorcaro, do Banco Master, e acusou o banqueiro de ter comprado autoridades. O ex-governador não apresentou provas dessa acusação.

“As pessoas com quem esse banqueiro, o senhor Vorcaro, encontrou são as mais altas figuras da República, com quem ele tomou uísque, com quem viajou no jatinho, deu carona, deu festas, convidou, conviveu e comprou”, afirmou.

Faixa de Zema em prédio da Paulista contra ministros do STF — Foto: TV Globo

Outra proposta apresentada por Zema foi acabar com as decisões monocráticas — aquelas tomadas individualmente por um ministro, sem análise do plenário ou de uma das turmas do Supremo.

“Quero também acabar com as decisões monocráticas. Vamos ter que debater: a assinatura de um ministro do Supremo valer mais do que a de 50 senadores ou de 400 deputados? Será que isso é democracia ou é outra coisa?”, questionou.

Zema também defendeu tornar públicos compromissos realizados pelo presidente da República dentro e fora do Palácio do Planalto, além de ligações telefônicas.

“Tudo o que o presidente tiver de agenda na casa dele ou no Palácio do Planalto tem de ser público, até ligações telefônicas”, disse.

Segundo ele, parentes do presidente e de ocupantes dos cargos mais altos do governo também deveriam informar atividades que pudessem gerar conflito de interesses.

Ao ser questionado se temia alguma consequência pela colocação da faixa na Avenida Paulista, Zema respondeu que não tinha “medo de prisão” e voltou a criticar autoridades em Brasília.

articles.title: Bebê viraliza nas redes em vídeo em que parece responder 'bom dia' | G1
articles.standfirst: O vídeo de família de Pouso Alegre superou 1 milhão de visualizações.
articles.summary: O vídeo de família de Pouso Alegre superou 1 milhão de visualizações.
articles.body:
Um bebê de apenas três meses virou sensação nas redes sociais depois que um vídeo em que ele parece responder “bom dia” à irmã viralizou. A postagem já ultrapassou 1 milhão de visualizações e chamou a atenção pela aparente precisão do som emitido pelo pequeno Otávio.

A família de Otávio mora em Pouso Alegre (MG). No vídeo, a irmã dele, Ana Júlia, cumprimenta o bebê: "Oi, bom dia". Em seguida, Otávio emite um som que se assemelha muito ao “bom dia” dito pela irmã, causando espanto nos participantes do vídeo.

Ana Júlia contou que costuma gravar vídeos do irmão desde que ele nasceu, principalmente enquanto ele balbucia e interage com a família.

Vídeo em que o pequeno Otávio, de três meses, parece responder "bom dia" à irmã viraliza nas redes — Foto: Reprodução redes sociais

“Foi a primeira vez que ele pronunciou tão certinho uma palavra. Eu achei muito fofo e falei: ‘Vou ter que salvar esse vídeo’.”

A intenção inicial, no entanto, não era publicar o vídeo nas redes sociais. Ana Júlia disse que queria apenas enviar o registro para uma amiga e mostrar para a mãe.

“Eu não queria nem postar. Eu queria mostrar para minha mãe para ver se eu estava ficando louca ou se realmente eu tinha ouvido o bom dia.”

A repercussão do vídeo fez com que profissionais comentassem a cena.

Segundo a mãe de Otávio, Juliana Paes Salvaterra, a avaliação é de que o bebê não teria propriamente respondido ao cumprimento, mas reproduzido o som que havia acabado de ouvir da irmã.

Independentemente das explicações técnicas, o momento já se tornou um dos mais especiais da breve vida de Otávio.

“Para a gente ele respondeu sim o bom dia. E foi o mais fofo", diz a mãe orgulhosa.

Juliana conta que Otávio é bastante comunicativo e costuma interagir principalmente com ela e com a irmã Ana Júlia, que participa da rotina do bebê desde os primeiros dias de vida.

“Depois de mim, a irmã é a segunda pessoa que mais convive com o Otávio, que mais estimula o Otávio, desde que ele chegou da maternidade”, conta a mãe.

Ana Júlia diz que, quando o irmão crescer, ela faz questão de contar sobre quando ele se tornou famoso.

“A gente vai conversar bastante e eu vou relembrar ele desse vídeo dele dando bom dia, que está viralizando na internet.”

articles.title: Mulher morre após levar choque em ventilador, diz Samu  | G1
articles.standfirst: Débora Santos, de 37 anos, recebeu uma descarga elétrica enquanto limpava a casa, em Itaberaí. Ela foi colocada na ambulância para ser levada ao hospital, mas sofreu uma nova parada cardíaca durante o trajeto.
articles.summary: Débora Santos, de 37 anos, recebeu uma descarga elétrica enquanto limpava a casa, em Itaberaí.
articles.body:
Débora Santos, de 37 anos, morreu após levar um choque elétrico enquanto limpava a casa, em Itaberaí , na Região Metropolitana de Goiânia. Segundo o Samu, ela recebeu a descarga no fio de um ventilador.

O marido acionou o socorro e chegou a fazer massagem cardíaca com orientação médica por videochamada.

Segundo o Samu, Débora foi colocada na ambulância para ser levada ao hospital, mas sofreu uma nova parada cardíaca durante o trajeto.

A morte foi confirmada na unidade de saúde. O corpo de Débora foi sepultado no domingo (6).

Débora morreu após levar um choque elêtrico — Foto: Reprodução/ TV Anhanguera

Amiga de Débora há cerca de quatro anos, Gabriella Monteiro, de 33 anos, contou ao g1 que conheceu a artesã como cliente e, depois, as duas desenvolveram uma amizade.

Segundo Gabriela, Débora produzia peças de artesanato, como flores, tiaras e laços. Ela também participava de feiras em Itaberaí e vendia os produtos pela internet para pessoas de outras cidades.

“A Débora era uma pessoa muito forte, muito amiga, muito determinada. Muito batalhadora, muito amiga, muito amada.”

Gabriela contou ainda que Débora era mãe de uma menina de 11 anos, que, segundo ela, é cardiopata. A amiga disse que a artesã estava empenhada em conseguir exames e tratamento para a filha.

articles.title: Acidente de paraglider em Sapiranga: homem cai no Morro Ferrabraz | G1
articles.standfirst: No último dia 23, um piloto de asa-delta ficou ferido após sofrer uma queda no mesmo local.
articles.summary: Um homem de 52 anos ficou gravemente ferido após um acidente de paraglider no Morro Ferrabraz, em Sapiranga, apenas duas semanas depois de outra queda registrada no local.
articles.body:
Acidente ocorreu em Sapiranga — Foto: Tiago Dal' Pizzol

Um homem de 52 anos ficou ferido após um acidente de paraglider no Morro Ferrabraz, em Sapiranga , na Região Metropolitana de Porto Alegre, na tarde desta segunda-feira (7). O Samu e os Bombeiros atendem a ocorrência. Não há informações sobre o estado de saúde ou a identidade do homem.

O paraglider, também chamado de parapente, é um equipamento leve e flexível usado para a prática de voo livre.

Segundo informações da Associação Gaúcha de Voo Livre (AGVL), durante o voo, uma rajada de vento teria provocado o fechamento do parapente, fazendo com que o piloto entrasse em queda livre.

Ainda conforme a associação, em uma situação como essa, o procedimento de segurança é acionar o parapente reserva. O piloto, que tinha cerca de um ano de experiência na modalidade, não teria conseguido realizar o procedimento.

O homem foi encaminhado ao Hospital de Sapiranga e está internado na Ala Vermelha.

No último dia 23, um piloto de asa-delta ficou ferido após sofrer uma queda no mesmo local. Segundo a AGVL, o acidente foi causado por uma turbulência na asa-delta no momento final do pouso. Ele caiu sobre um carro que passava na rua naquele instante.

articles.title: Homem é detido por agredir parentes após morte do pai em Boa Vista | G1
articles.standfirst: Suspeito de 25 anos chegou em casa embriagado e agrediu irmão e prima no bairro Operário. Polícia havia sido chamada ao local inicialmente para registrar óbito do pai dele.
articles.summary: Suspeito de 25 anos chegou em casa embriagado e agrediu irmão e prima no bairro Operário. Polícia havia sido chamada ao local inicialmente para registrar óbito do pai dele.
articles.body:
Polícia Militar de Roraima havia sido chamada ao local inicialmente para registrar óbito do pai do suspeito. — Foto: Vanessa Fernandes/g1 RR/Arquivo

Um homem de 25 anos foi detido na noite deste domingo (6) após agredir familiares com socos e chutes no bairro Operário, em Boa Vista . A confusão ocorreu em uma residência, momentos após a morte do pai do suspeito por causas naturais.

A PM foi acionada inicialmente para atender apenas a ocorrência de óbito, pois o homem falecido era um paciente em cuidados paliativos. No entanto, antes da chegada da equipe, o filho chegou ao local com sinais de embriaguez.

Visivelmente alterado, o jovem passou a atacar os parentes. Entre as vítimas do ataque estão a prima do suspeito, uma jovem de 21 anos, e o próprio irmão dele, um autônomo de 36 anos.

Para interromper a violência, o autônomo precisou segurar e imobilizar o irmão. Quando os policiais chegaram à casa, o suspeito continuava agressivo e precisou ser algemado por segurança.

Apesar das agressões, todos os envolvidos estavam sem ferimentos físicos aparentes. Eles foram levados à delegacia para os procedimentos legais, e o caso foi registrado como tentativa de lesão corporal dolosa .

articles.title: Gaza: Genocide in Real Time?
articles.summary: Gaza examined through occupation, blockade, mass killing and the genocide case before the ICJ.
articles.body:
Gaza examined through occupation, blockade, mass killing and the genocide case before the ICJ.

Gaza, seen through the legal and political framework of genocide, as allegations are argued in real time before international courts. This episode traces how decades of occupation, blockade and repeated wars created conditions of confinement, dependency and dehumanisation long before the war that began on October 7, 2023. It explores how displacement orders, siege tactics, destruction of infrastructure, and AI-assisted targeting have shaped the scale and pattern of killing and destruction. Drawing on testimony, military analysis and legal argument, the episode follows how Palestinian victims, Israel, and third states frame the intent and nature of the violence, and why the International Court of Justice has warned of a “plausible risk” of genocide without yet ruling on its commission. It asks what this unfolding legal battle means for accountability, future deterrence and the people of Gaza themselves.

articles.title: Mulher é presa levando drogas na mochila da filha de 8 anos no AP | G1
articles.standfirst: Revista foi gravada pela polícia e mostra o momento em que a criança entrega a mochila aos policiais. Suspeita disse que levava a droga a mando do marido, preso no Iapen.
articles.summary: Revista foi gravada pela polícia e mostra o momento em que a criança entrega a mochila aos policiais. Suspeita disse que levava a droga a mando do marido, preso no Iapen.
articles.body:
Uma mulher foi presa ao transportar drogas na mochila da filha de 8 anos, no bairro do Pacoval, na Zona Norte de Macapá . Os entorpecentes estavam escondidos entre roupas e itens de higiene. A abordagem foi registrada em vídeo pela Companhia de Patrulhamento Tático com Apoio de Motocicletas (Patamo).

A mulher disse que as porções de crack pertenciam ao marido, preso por tráfico no Instituto de Administração Penitenciária do Amapá (Iapen). Segundo ela, recebeu ordem para entregar a droga em troca de dinheiro.

O flagrante ocorreu na sexta-feira (4). A polícia informou que a mulher dirigia de forma suspeita e tentou manobras arriscadas ao perceber a aproximação da equipe.

Ainda segundo a polícia, sem ser questionada, a mulher confessou que a droga estava na mochila carregada pela filha.

No vídeo, a criança aparece abraçada à mochila e depois a entrega espontaneamente aos policiais. A mulher também entregou outra porção de drogas que estava em sua roupa. Dinheiro em espécie também foi apreendido.

Mulher confessou que o material estava na mochila — Foto: Patamo/Divulgação

A mulher chorou e demonstrou estar abalada quando a droga foi encontrada.

A mulher e a filha foram levadas ao Centro Integrado de Operações em Segurança Pública (Ciosp) do Pacoval. O Conselho Tutelar foi acionado e a criança entregue a um familiar indicado pela mãe.

A suspeita foi encaminhada para audiência de custódia.

Material foi apresentado no Ciosp do Pacoval — Foto: Polícia MilitarDivulgação

articles.title: Acidente com caminhão em Cosmópolis: casas têm risco de desabamento | G1
articles.standfirst: Acidente ocorreu na tarde deste domingo (6) em Cosmópolis (SP). Casas têm risco de desabamento de lajes, segundo Defesa Civil.
articles.summary: A Defesa Civil de Cosmópolis isolou imóveis com risco de desabamento após um acidente com caminhão atingir três casas e três veículos no domingo.
articles.body:
A Defesa Civil de Cosmópolis (SP) informou, nesta segunda-feira (7), que existe risco de desabamento nas casas atingidas pelo caminhão desgovernado na tarde deste domingo (6). Moradores relataram o susto no momento do acidente. "Pensei que fosse trovão" , disse um morador. "Achei que fosse bomba", contou o dono de dois carros levados pela carreta.

Uma das residências ficou mais destruída e, segundo o órgão, oferece mais risco de queda da laje. Por isso, as equipes da perícia permanecem no local, que está isolado, é tem necessidade de escoramento, antes de fazer a retirada da carreta. Uma latinha de cerveja foi encontrada na cabine do caminhão.

Valdemiro Carvalho, que mora no imóvel com a esposa, filha e neto há cerca de 20 anos, diz ter se assustado com o acidente, pelo estrondo com o impacto da batida. “Foi que nem um trovão, a minha mulher falou: 'e esse trovão nessa hora?’", lembrou.

“Quando eu olhei ali de cima, foi que eu vi o carro. O carro dentro, falei ‘acabou com a casa’. Nós descemos para ver o menino. O menino estava mais para lá, não teve nada não”, disse a respeito da criança, que ficou na parte de baixo da casa.

Outras duas casas e três veículos também foram atingidos - dois estacionados na rua e um que estava dentro da garagem do imóvel que ficou mais destruído.

Danos estruturais: durante a vistoria da Defesa Civil, foi constatada a existência de danos na estrutura dos imóveis atingidos.

"Conforme avaliação realizada no local, qualquer movimentação do caminhão ou retirada do veículo sem os devidos cuidados e procedimentos técnicos poderá ocasionar o comprometimento e eventual colapso das estruturas das residências atingidas, sendo necessária a adoção de medidas de segurança e acompanhamento técnico para a remoção do veículo", detalhou a prefeitura.

Caminhão bate em muro de casa e veículos estacionados em Cosmópolis — Foto: Guarda Civil de Cosmópolis/Reprodução

Vizinho da família, Clemilton de Jesus é o dono dos dois carros atingidos e que estavam estacionados na rua. Ele também estava em casa no momento do acidente e pensou que o barulho era de uma bomba.

“Cheguei por volta de umas 3h50, 3h40. Entrei, 10 minutinhos, 15 minutinhos, eu ouvi um barulho. Isso aqui é bomba. Eu nem imaginava que ia ser uma batida de carro. Quando eu saí, eu me assustei. Eu já vi meus dois carros batidos. Aí eu fui na casa do vizinho, o caminhão, a caçamba entrou na casa do vizinho”, disse.

Caminhão destrói muro de casa; motorista ficou ferido — Foto: Arquivo pessoal

Segundo Clemilton, ele abordou o motorista.

“Quando eu voltei para olhar o meu carro, o cara desceu.Falei, ‘o que aconteceu, irmão?’ Ele falou ‘bebo, bebo, bebo’”.

“Ele se evadiu, ele saiu, foi sentido mercado. Aí eu corri, peguei no braço dele e falei, ‘não, vai resolver o meu problema. Depois você vai embora’. Aí ele falou, ‘não, irmão, liga para a minha esposa’. Eu peguei o meu telefone, liguei primeiro para o 190”, afirmou.

Imagens de câmeras de circuito de segurança flagraram o momento em que o caminhão desgovernado bate contra o muro da casa e atinge os carros em Cosmópolis (SP) . Veja, abaixo.

O motorista sofreu escoriações, foi socorrido e levado para hospital da cidade. Segundo a Defesa Civil da cidade, a estrutra do imóvel ficou comprometida. Outros imóveis também foram atingidos.

As imagens flagraram o acidente em dois ângulos diferentes. No primeiro, é possível ver o caminhão virando a esquina e se aproximando da residência, desgovernado. Em outro registro, a câmera flagra o impacto do veículo contra o muro da residência e os outros carros estacionados na rua.

Caminhão desgovernado bate contra carros estacionados, muro de casa e compromete estrutura de imóvel em Cosmópolis — Foto: Guarda Civil de Cosmópolis/Reprodução

O acidente ocorreu na Avenida Severino Beraldo, que fica perto do limite entre Cosmópolis e Paulínia (SP). Segundo a Guarda Municipal de Cosmópolis, houve briga com agressão entre a família do caminhoneiro e moradores do bairro.

O caminhão seguia pela Estrada da Granja. Ao fazer uma conversão à direita para acessar a Rua Severino Beraldo, o motorista perdeu o controle da direção, subiu no canteiro central e, depois, bateu contra três veículos e três casas.

O motorista sofreu escoriações e foi encaminhado para atendimento médico, aponta nota da Secretaria de Segurança Pública (SSP) de São Paulo. A perícia foi acionada.A ocorrência foi registrada como colisão e dano na Delegacia de Polícia de Cosmópolis.

O primeiro veículo atingido foi um Chevrolet Montana, que estava estacionado. Na sequência, o caminhão bateu contra um Peugeot 207. Os dois veículos pertencem a mesma pessoa.

O caminhão também atingiu um Fiat dentro da garagem da casa.

A CPFL Paulista informa que uma equipe esteve no local e constatou que o caminhão atingiu apenas o padrão de entrada do cliente. O fornecimento de energia no local não foi impactado.

Segundo o Corpo de Bombeiros, o motorista foi socorrido por uma ambulância do município.

articles.title: Super El Niño: temperatura média pode subir até 2°C em regiões | G1
articles.standfirst: Fenômeno também poderá motivar a formação de temporais violentos. Outras áreas do interior paulista e do sul de Minas Gerais também enfrentarão calor atípico.
articles.summary: Fenômeno também poderá motivar a formação de temporais violentos. Outras áreas do interior paulista e do sul de Minas Gerais também enfrentarão calor atípico.
articles.body:
O Super El Niño , fenômeno climático conhecido por favorecer ondas de calor, deverá aumentar em 2°C a temperatura média das regiões de Campinas (SP) e de Piracicaba (SP). A projeção foi informada pelo Centro de Previsão do Tempo e Estudos Climáticos (Cptec) à EPTV , emissora afiliada da TV Globo .

🌊 Entenda: O El Niño é caracterizado pelo aumento anormal da temperatura da superfície do Oceano Pacífico, na região próxima à Linha do Equador, o que deixa a atmosfera mais aquecida e diminui a frequência e a intensidade das ondas de frio.

Ainda de acordo com o Cptec, outras áreas do interior paulista e do sul de Minas Gerais também enfrentarão calor atípico:

Região de Ribeirão Preto (SP): aumento de 2,5°C na temperatura média

Região de São Carlos (SP): aumento de 2°C

Região do sul de Minas Gerais: aumento de 1,8°C

"Parece pouco. Por quê? Porque, na verdade, a gente vai ter essas oscilações entre períodos muito quentes e de chuva. Nesses períodos muito quentes, os picos de temperatura podem fazer com que a gente fique até mais de 5°C acima da média", disse Giovanni Dolif, pesquisador e coordenador de operações do Centro Nacional de Monitoramento e Alertas de Desastres Naturais (Cemaden).

Já em todo o Brasil, a tendência é que o Super El Niño aumente o risco de seca no norte e no nordeste. Ao mesmo tempo, as frentes frias que vêm da Argentina e do Uruguai ficam bloqueadas no sul do país, podendo provocar mais chuvas nessa área.

"Se as frentes frias ficam bloqueadas no sul do Brasil, elas não chegam à região sudeste. Ou se chegam, chegam com menos intensidade. Por isso que as temperaturas ficam mais altas na região sudeste, principalmente em São Paulo, Rio de Janeiro e Minas Gerais", explicou Gilvan Sampaio de Oliveira, pesquisador do Instituto Nacional de Pesquisas Espaciais (Inpe).

Campinas pode ter sofrer com impactos do El Niño — Foto: Carlos Bassan/Prefeitura de Campinas

A intensidade do El Niño pode ser medida pelo aquecimento do oceano. Das últimas 10 ocorrências do fenômeno desde 1982, o recorde de aumento da temperatura do Pacífico Equatorial foi em 1997, com 3,24°C.

Neste ano, a temperatura do oceano ainda está subindo, mas com 2,3°C acima do normal, já supera os registros para essa época de todas as outras ocorrências . "Nós estamos evoluindo para talvez o El Niño mais intenso já registrado", afirmou Gilvan.

O calor intenso provocado pelo Super El Niño é o principal combustível para a formação de temporais violentos. Giovanni explicou que os ventos fortes em grandes altitudes sugam o ar quente e úmido da superfície, fazendo com que as tempestades se desenvolvam mais rápido e durem mais tempo .

O resultado desse processo são as chamadas microexplosões, quando o ar frio desce das nuvens com grande violência. Segundo o especialista do Cemaden, os ventos gerados por esse evento podem atingir até 200 km/h , trazendo alto potencial destrutivo para as cidades.

Um fenômeno semelhante atingiu Ribeirão Preto em julho de 2026, quando ventos atingiram 160 km/h. Moradora da Favela da Paz, a atendente de telemarketing Ana Laura dos Santos relembrou o desespero de ver a água invadir a residência.

"A maioria [das telhas] voou e o que não voou, abaixou, reclinou essa parte aqui e tudo alagou", relatou.

Estragos causados por temporal severo em Ribeirão Preto (SP) — Foto: Reprodução/EPTV

A desempregada Maria Eduarda Bonfim também precisou agir rápido para proteger a família durante a ventania. "Com o vento, levantou todo o telhado. Aí eu catei eles [os filhos], corri para dentro do banheiro, peguei uma cobertinha que foi a única coisa que eu salvei", contou.

Para Gilvan, a intensidade do fenômeno atual exige adaptação da sociedade. Ele ainda ressaltou que as mudanças climáticas estão sendo agravadas pelo aquecimento global.

"Nós temos de tomar medidas para esse novo normal, com chuvas intensas, com ondas de calor, temperaturas mais altas", concluiu.

O forte calor favorecido pelo Super El Niño pode afetar a população de várias formas. Alguns desses impactos são indiretos, como, por exemplo, o aumento da conta de energia elétrica. Confira abaixo alguns dos impactos.

🌱 Agricultura: em anos de El Niño há um aumento nos preços de frutas e hortaliças por conta das fortes chuvas ou do calor extremo, que colocam em risco a produção agrícola;

⚡ Energia elétrica: há um maior consumo tanto de água, que é fundamental para a produção de energia no país, quanto da própria energia — ar-condicionado ou mais banhos por dia, por exemplo;

🔥 Queimadas: com o tempo seco, aumenta a possibilidade de desenvolvimento de queimadas naturais. Quando há alguma ação humana, o incêndio fica mais fácil de se alastrar e causar prejuízos ambientais;

🏥 Saúde: a quantidade de atendimentos por desidratação ou por outros efeitos do calor extremo pode aumentar, principalmente para idosos e pessoas com comorbidades. As recomendações às pessoas e aos animais de estimação são evitar exposição direta e prolongada à radiação solar, bem como manter hidratação.

articles.summary: Série reúne três mapas lançados entre 2024 e 2026, com Brasil centralizado, Sul no topo e uma versão que destaca a biodiversidade.
articles.body:
Mapa-múndi Riqueza das Espécies com Brasil no centro. — Foto: IBGE

O IBGE liberou nesta segunda-feira (7), em celebração ao Dia da Independência , o acesso a uma série de três mapas-múndi lançados entre 2024 e 2026.

Os arquivos podem ser baixados gratuitamente pela loja virtual do instituto. Para fazer o download, é necessário entrar na conta ou criar um cadastro no site ( clique aqui para acessar ).

A loja também oferece versões impressas de alguns mapas para compra.

A série começou em 2024, com um mapa-múndi que coloca o Brasil no centro da representação. A versão foi lançada durante a presidência brasileira do G20 .

Mapa-múndi - O Brasil no Mundo G20. — Foto: IBGE

No ano seguinte, o IBGE apresentou um segundo mapa, também com o Brasil centralizado, mas com o Hemisfério Sul na parte de cima. O material foi divulgado durante a presidência brasileira do Brics.

Já este ano, o instituto lançou o mapa-múndi “ Riqueza de Espécies 2025 ”, que mantém o Brasil no centro e o Sul no topo, mas destaca a distribuição da biodiversidade em diferentes regiões do planeta.

Segundo o IBGE, os mapas fazem parte de uma série que busca apresentar diferentes formas de representação cartográfica e chamar atenção para as escolhas envolvidas na elaboração de um mapa.

Algumas das versões usam a projeção Equal Earth , adotada para representar de forma mais equilibrada as proporções das áreas dos continentes. Este mês, a Assembleia Geral das Nações Unidas aprovou uma resolução favorável ao uso dessa projeção.

“Ao adotar a Equal Earth, centralizar o Brasil e experimentar a inversão da orientação convencional Norte–Sul, o Instituto passou a explicitar que toda representação cartográfica resulta de escolhas técnicas e convencionais”, afirmou o presidente do IBGE, Marcio Pochmann.

A diretora de Geociências do instituto, Maria do Carmo Bueno, disse que a decisão da ONU reforça a discussão sobre diferentes formas de representar o planeta.

Os três mapas podem ser acessados na Loja do IBGE , que também reúne outras publicações e produtos cartográficos do instituto ( acesse aqui ).

articles.title: Satya Niketan deadly deja vu: 4 years apart, 2 building collapses in same South Delhi lane - the warning nobody acted on
articles.summary: Four years apart, meters apart — two building collapses in the same south Delhi neighbourhood, both linked to construction or renovation work and both.
articles.body: Four years apart, meters apart — two building collapses in the same south Delhi neighbourhood, both linked to construction or renovation work and both raising the same uncomfortable question: What happens when warnings are issued but enforcement does not follow?On April 25, 2022, a three-storey building in Satya Niketan collapsed during renovation work, killing two labourers and injuring four others. The structure had already been declared dangerous by the municipal corporation on March 31. Police had also been asked to stop the work.Yet, before the civic action could be completed, the building came crashing down.Four years later, on September 6, 2026, another building collapsed in the same south Delhi neighbourhood. This time, the five-storey structure housed a student paying guest accommodation. At least seven people were killed and several others injured.The two incidents are separated by four years but by only a few metres — and the 2022 collapse now offers an uncomfortable glimpse into the warnings that had already existed about the dangers of construction and structural alterations in Satya Niketan.2022: A dangerous building, a notice and a collapseDelhi Fire Services received a call around 1.25pm reporting that a three-storey building in Satya Niketan had collapsed. At least five labourers were initially feared trapped beneath the rubble.Police, fire services, the National Disaster Response Force and the power distribution company launched a rescue operation. Five trapped labourers were eventually pulled out and taken to hospital.Two of them — Naseem, 35, and Bilal, 40 — died. Four others were injured.But the collapse was not entirely without warning.According to the South Delhi Municipal Corporation, the building had been declared dangerous on March 31, nearly a month before the collapse. The civic body had issued a notice to the owner against carrying out additions and alterations to the property.Police intervention had also been sought to stop the work.The building was around 25 years old and stood on a 90-square-yard plot. According to the civic body, the owner was carrying out additions and alterations when the structure suddenly collapsed.The SDMC mayor at the time, Mukkesh Suryaan, said construction was being carried out without permission and promised an inquiry into the role of the owner and officials, if any lapses were found.An SDMC official, however, said the civic body had followed the procedure prescribed under the rules.The official said the corporation was waiting for the notice period to end and that proceedings had been completed only days before the collapse. Action with the help of police had been planned for the following week.The building collapsed before that action could happen.A neighbourhood built around old structuresSatya Niketan, close to Delhi University’s South Campus, has long been a densely built residential and student hub.The area is made up of narrow lanes lined with houses, paying guest accommodations, eateries and small commercial establishments. Many of the properties are old, while some have undergone additions or alterations over the years.After the 2022 collapse, residents had pointed to the structural vulnerabilities of buildings in the area.Locals said many houses had been constructed without pillars and that additional floors had subsequently been added to old structures.The collapse also highlighted the pressure placed on such buildings by the area's transformation into a major student accommodation hub.The victims in 2022 were labourers working at the site.Naseem had worked as a labourer in Delhi for nearly two decades and was survived by his wife, four daughters and a son in Bihar.Bilal had been working at the site for around 20 days. His brother said Bilal had worked in Delhi for five years and his wife and five children were in Bihar.For their families, the collapse was not simply a story about a building or a municipal notice. It was the loss of breadwinners who had gone to work that afternoon.Four years later, another collapseOn September 6, 2026, Satya Niketan again became a rescue zone.A five-storey building housing students as paying guests collapsed in the afternoon, trapping people beneath tonnes of concrete.The structure came down in what fire officials described as a pancake collapse, with floors crashing onto one another and leaving slabs stacked across the building.Students who lived in the building alleged it had been vacated the previous year for being too run-down to inhabit safely. The MCD, students say, later cleared the same structure to operate as a 75-bed PG accommodation anyway.At least seven people died.Students were among those trapped. Families rushed to the site and hospitals searching for relatives. Residents, student groups and emergency personnel worked through the rubble as rescue teams tried to reach those still alive.Some trapped students were able to communicate from beneath the debris.The rescue operation was complicated by the weight and instability of the collapsed structure. Fire officials said heavy machinery could not immediately be used because it could endanger people trapped underneath.Once again, questions about construction and structural safety quickly surfaced.Investigators began examining whether repair or renovation work had been carried out in the building, including work in the basement and ground floor, and whether such activity contributed to the collapse.MCD officials also began examining the building's structural condition and its use as a PG accommodation.The question that 2022 left behindThe two collapses cannot automatically be treated as the same failure.There is no basis to say that the 2022 incident directly caused the 2026 collapse, or that the later building was necessarily the same structure that had been declared dangerous four years earlier.But the proximity of the two incidents makes the earlier case difficult to ignore.In 2022, authorities had already encountered a dangerous building in Satya Niketan where construction work was allegedly continuing despite civic intervention.A notice had been issued.Police had been asked to stop the work.The civic body said proceedings were underway.But the building collapsed before the planned enforcement action could take place.Four years later, another structure in the same neighbourhood collapsed, killing students and workers and once again putting construction, structural safety and oversight under scrutiny.The question, therefore, is larger than one building.It is whether the lessons from the first collapse translated into sustained enforcement across a neighbourhood where old residential structures have increasingly been converted into student accommodation and commercial premises.A warning is only as effective as the action that followsThe 2022 tragedy had already exposed a familiar problem in Delhi's built environment: Authorities may identify dangerous structures and issue notices, but the gap between identifying a violation and physically preventing unsafe work can prove fatal.The official explanation in 2022 was that the prescribed process was being followed and that enforcement action was imminent.Now, after seven deaths in another Satya Niketan collapse, the old question has returned with greater force.How many dangerous structures are identified?How many notices are issued?How many are actually vacated, sealed or demolished before tragedy strikes?And most importantly, when a building is declared dangerous, who ensures that people do not continue working or living inside it while paperwork runs its course?Four years ago, Satya Niketan gave warning.Four years later, the neighbourhood has suffered another deadly collapse.The distance between the two sites may be measured in meters. articles.title: After owner Hariram’s arrest, Delhi Police arrest wife, son in Satya Niketan building collapse
articles.summary: NEW DELHI: Delhi Police have arrested the alleged owner of the building that collapsed in Satya Niketan, along with his wife and son, in connection wi.
articles.body: NEW DELHI: Delhi Police have arrested the alleged owner of the building that collapsed in Satya Niketan, along with his wife and son, in connection with the incident that left seven people dead.Police identified the three as Hariram Gupta, his wife Urmila and their son Mahesh.According to Delhi Police, the electricity connection of the building was in Hariram's name, while the property was registered on paper in the name of his wife, Urmila.Their son Mahesh was handling the management of the property, news agency ANI reported. Hariram was earlier apprehended in BhiwadiHariram had earlier been apprehended in Bhiwadi after he remained untraceable following the building collapse.Delhi Police had formed 10 teams comprising personnel from district police, the Special Staff and other operational units to trace him. An FIR had also been registered against him and a Look Out Circular (LOC) was issued.The collapse has claimed seven lives, while 13 people were rescued from the debris. Rescue operations continued at the site as teams searched for any remaining victims. Five MCD officials suspended after collapseFollowing the collapse, the Delhi government suspended five MCD officials, including the Deputy Commissioner of the South Zone, Superintending Engineer, Executive Engineer, Assistant Engineer and Junior Engineer.MCD Commissioner Sanjeev Khirwar said an adjoining building had also weakened and was being strengthened before being demolished in a calibrated manner over the next one to two days.“In August, we had passed demolition orders for 3-4 buildings in the same area. A regular identification is conducted. In the last three months, 960 demolitions were carried out, 407 buildings were sealed, and notices were served to 1,500 buildings for sealing and demolition,” Khirwar said.He said the action was part of the MCD's regular drive against unauthorised construction. Protests, demands for safer PG accommodationThe collapse triggered protests by students affiliated with the NSUI and ABVP, who demanded accountability and stronger safety measures for students living in paying guest accommodations.Jhanvi Kataria, a DUSU 2026 election candidate, demanded construction of hostels for students and said the government should bear their PG and flat rents until land is allocated for such facilities.She also pointed to a similar building collapse in the area three years ago and questioned why adequate precautions had not been taken to prevent a recurrence.Congress leader Srinivas BV accused the government of delaying its response to the collapse and alleged that government rescue teams took three hours to reach the site. He claimed NSUI members helped rescue people before official teams arrived. Adjoining structures evacuated amid safety concernsThe incident also raised concerns over the safety of neighbouring structures.Authorities evacuated buildings in the vicinity after cracks were reported in some structures, while iron jacks were installed to support nearby buildings.Chief Minister Rekha Gupta directed officials to immediately seal illegal five-storey buildings across Delhi and ordered intensive inspections of PG accommodations and other buildings in the area.The government has said strict action will be taken against MCD officials found responsible for any lapses.(With agency inputs)You Can Also Check: Gold Rate in Delhi | Silver Rate in Delhi | Bank Holidays in Delhi | Public Holidays in Delhi | Delhi AQI | Weather in Delhi | Petrol Price in Delhi | Diesel Price in Delhi | CNG Price in Delhi | LPG Price in DelhiStay updated with the latest Delhi news. articles.title: In 2022, millionaire couple bought dream home in Kent. Three years later, they are suing previous owners as noisy travelers with 16 children moved in neighborhood
articles.summary: UK News: It was supposed to be the kind of country retreat most people could only dream of: a five-bedroom manor-style house set across seven acres, complete w.
articles.body: It was supposed to be the kind of country retreat most people could only dream of: a five-bedroom manor-style house set across seven acres, complete with a swimming pool, tennis court, paddocks, stables and even a private helipad. Jamie and Eda Pierce thought they had found their perfect escape from the chaos of everyday life when they bought the sprawling property in Pootings, a hamlet near Crockham Hill in Kent, for £3.15 million in August 2022. According to a Daily Mail report, the couple had even negotiated a £245,000 reduction from the asking price.But three years later, their idyllic countryside life had turned into a legal nightmare. And in a twist, the couple are not suing the travellers who moved into a field opposite their home. They are taking the previous owners to court, accusing them of concealing a crucial piece of information before the £3.15 million sale.'Previous owners knew but they did not disclose'The Pierces alleged that the former owners, Paul and Elizabeth Nott, knew that a neighbouring agricultural plot was at risk of being developed for traveller accommodation but failed to disclose it.The couple has now launched a multi-million-pound High Court action, alleging fraudulent misrepresentation and deceit.According to their legal claim, the Pierces had specifically asked before buying whether the sellers knew of any plans to alter, develop or change the use of neighbouring land within a quarter of a mile of the property.Their solicitor was allegedly told: “Not to our clients’ knowledge.” The Pierces claimed that answer was false.What made the allegation particularly significant, according to court documents cited by the Daily Mail, is that the previous owner, Paul Nott, allegedly knew considerably more about the neighbouring land than the response suggested.Previous owner's unsuccessful bid to buy landIn 2021, months before the Pierces purchased the property, locals had reportedly become concerned about the sale of a six-acre agricultural plot known as Seasons Farm.The documents claimed Nott and another resident attempted to buy the land themselves in September 2021 in an effort to prevent what they regarded as unwanted development. Their offer was rejected and the property was subsequently sold to Patrick Delaney.Nott allegedly became involved in efforts by local residents to oppose possible development of the site. He was reportedly a founder member of the Pootings Residents’ Association, which was formed in February 2022 to fight the proposals.Around the same time, in spring 2022, the Pierces said the Notts put their own property on the market. The couple eventually bought it that August.Then came the development they say they had never been warned about. After moving into their dream home, Delaney reportedly made several unsuccessful attempts to change the use of Seasons Farm from agricultural to residential.Land finally sold but to four traveler familiesIn July 2025, the land was sold to four traveller families. On August 22, 2025, shortly after 5pm and just before the bank holiday weekend, the families arrived.According to the account cited by the Mail, trucks, excavators, caravans and mobile homes descended on the site. Hedgerows were removed, an entrance and driveway were created and tarmac was laid. Water and electricity infrastructure, sewage facilities, fencing and other works were installed within hours.By the time a High Court injunction was served on Sunday morning, much of the work had already been completed.Four families, including 16 children, had moved onto the six-acre site.For residents of Pootings, a hamlet of only around 60 people living in 27 properties, the sudden arrival transformed the character of the area almost overnight.Locals have complained of machinery and quad-bike noise, intrusive floodlights and disturbances at unsociable hours. Some residents have also alleged that attempts to challenge the activity were met with intimidation.The travellers were later found in contempt of court for breaching court orders, while a retrospective planning application for the site was rejected by Sevenoaks District Council in May 2026.For the Pierces, however, the battle has moved beyond planning.Their barrister, Jonathan Seitler KC, told the court that had the couple known the development was likely, they would never have bought the property.The couple now claimed that their home has effectively become worthless to them. They were seeking to have the sale contract rescinded and want the £3.15 million purchase price returned, along with money spent on the property, damages, interest, stamp duty and legal costs.Their once-open country estate has reportedly been transformed into something resembling a fortress, with security cameras, high wooden gates and warning signs.The case has yet to be decided, and the allegations against the former owners remain unproven. Paul and Elizabeth Nott have not yet filed a response to the legal claim and declined to comment when contacted by the Daily Mail.For the Pierces, what began as the purchase of a secluded country dream has become a fight over a question that could determine whether their £3.15 million investment was built on a hidden warning they were never told about.Catch the latest World News and Live updates. articles.title: Why has Nicaragua taken Germany to the ICJ over Gaza genocide?
articles.summary: Nicaragua accuses Germany of violating the Genocide Convention by supporting Israel amid its onslaught on Gaza.
articles.body:
Germany is back before the International Court of Justice (ICJ) at The Hague over its support for Israel, more than two years after Nicaragua accused Berlin of “facilitating” the Gaza genocide by supplying Israel with weapons.

Filed in 2024, the case alleges Germany has breached the Genocide Convention and international humanitarian law.

Germany, Israel’s biggest arms supplier after the US, denies the accusations and is seeking to stop the case from proceeding, challenging the admissibility of some of Nicaragua’s claims, as well as the court’s jurisdiction.

The ICJ, or World Court as it is widely known, which was set up to rule in disputes between nations, has become a key player in Israel’s genocide in Gaza, following the Hamas-led October 7, 2024 attacks. A case of genocide brought by South Africa against Israel is ongoing.

The hearings in the Netherlands do not yet decide whether Germany, Europe’s largest economy, violated international law. They will determine whether the case can move towards a fuller examination of the allegations.

Nicaragua says Germany has violated its obligations under the 1948 Genocide Convention by providing Israel with military equipment, despite being aware of the risk that genocide could be committed in Gaza.

It has also accused Germany of breaching international humanitarian law.

“By sending military equipment and now defunding UNRWA … Germany is facilitating the commission of genocide,” Nicaragua said when it filed the case in March 2024.

Germany has long been one of Israel’s strongest international supporters, despite widespread acknowledgement from human rights groups and top genocide scholars that Israel is committing genocide in the Palestinian territory.

Carlos Jose Arguello Gomez, Nicaragua’s ambassador to the Netherlands, argued in 2024 that Germany had failed “to differentiate between self-defence and genocide”.

Nicaragua initially sought emergency orders requiring Germany to halt military assistance to Israel and resume funding for UNRWA.

However, the ICJ rejected those provisional measures in April 2024, but refused to dismiss the broader case.

In January 2024, the World Court ruled – as part of a separate case brought by South Africa – that there was “a real and imminent risk that irreparable prejudice” would be caused to the rights of Palestinians in Gaza under the Genocide Convention.

Germany rejects Nicaragua’s allegations and has asked the court to throw out the case.

On Monday, Germany told the ICJ that Nicaragua had failed to follow the required steps before bringing the case, and that large parts of its complaint lie beyond the court’s jurisdiction under the Genocide Convention.

“Germany ⁠⁠⁠⁠respectfully requests the court to reject Nicaragua’s claims,” legal adviser of the German foreign ministry, Julia Monar, told the court’s judges.

Berlin has argued that its weapons exports undergo detailed legal scrutiny.

During the 2024 hearings, German lawyer Christian Tams said 98 percent of exports to Israel since October 7, 2023, consisted of general military equipment such as helmets, vests and binoculars.

Germany is now making “preliminary objections”, arguing that the ICJ lacks jurisdiction and that some of Nicaragua’s claims are inadmissible. The full details of those objections have not been made public.

A US-brokered ceasefire has been in place since last October, but Israeli attacks have continued.

Israeli attacks killed at least four Palestinians on Sunday, including an eight-year-old girl and a three-year-old boy.

Gaza’s Ministry of Health says at least 1,344 Palestinians have been killed and 4,464 wounded since the ceasefire took effect. The ministry puts the overall Palestinian death toll since October 2023 at 73,470, with at least 174,540 wounded.

The UN Satellite Centre says 82 percent of Gaza’s buildings have been damaged or destroyed, while Gaza health authorities, UN agencies and aid groups estimate that 10,000 to 14,000 people remain missing beneath rubble.

How long will the case take to conclude?

The immediate jurisdictional dispute could be decided much sooner than the overall case.

The ICJ is holding four days of hearings, after which judges must decide whether Germany succeeds in having the case thrown out. Such preliminary rulings take an average of about six months.

If Germany loses this stage, Nicaragua’s allegations would move towards consideration “on the merits” – a process that can take years.

For comparison, in South Africa’s separate genocide case against Israel, the ICJ has given South Africa until November 2027 for written pleadings and Israel until May 2029 to respond, meaning hearings on whether Israel committed genocide are unlikely before late 2029 at the earliest.

There is therefore no firm date for a final judgement in Nicaragua’s case against Germany – and, if it survives Berlin’s current challenge, a conclusion could still be years away.

articles.title: Iraq faces sovereignty test as US-led military coalition exit nears
articles.summary: Analysts warn Iraq faces severe security and political tests as the US-led coalition withdrawal deadline approaches.
articles.body:
The United States-led international military coalition will conclude its mission in Iraq by the end of this month, the country’s armed forces have confirmed to state media.

Lieutenant General Abdul Amir al-Shammari, director of the Office of the Commander-in-Chief of the Armed Forces, in a statement to the Iraqi News Agency on Monday, said September 30 is the date for the end of the mission of the international coalition forces in Iraq and the transition to a new chapter of relations and cooperation.

Earlier, Iraqi Prime Minister Ali al-Zaidi’s security adviser, Qasim al-Araji, had confirmed that the US-led international military coalition would conclude its mission in the country this month.

Under a 2024 agreement between Baghdad and Washington, the withdrawal includes the removal of US air defence systems stationed in Erbil, the capital of the autonomous Kurdish region in Iraq.

These platforms have been critical to the interception of Iranian ballistic missiles and drones targeting the region amid the US-Israel war on Iran.

US forces led the invasion of Iraq in 2003, which resulted in a bloody civil war in the country, with approximately 200,000 civilians killed in war-related violence. After withdrawing from Iraq in 2011, US forces returned in 2015, as part of an international coalition fighting the ISIL (ISIS) group.

“September 30 will be the fixed and final date for ending the military mission of the Global Coalition to Defeat ISIS in Iraq and completing the departure of its forces,” the prime minister’s office said.

“October 1 will mark a new day in the trajectory of the Iraqi state, as Iraq will be free of any foreign military presence … [The move] represents an essential prerequisite for moving Iraq into a new phase of development and prosperity.”

Iyad al-Anbar, a political science professor at the University of Baghdad, told Al Jazeera that the military withdrawal is largely a formality.

“I believe this issue is almost agreed upon. Fundamentally, the concentration of US forces in Iraq is no longer in military barracks or Iraqi military bases, but has become concentrated in the Harir base in Erbil,” al-Anbar told Al Jazeera. “Ultimately, this issue will be mostly symbolic, considering that the Americans have ended their military presence in many headquarters where they used to be; even in Camp Victory near Baghdad airport and others, the support base, and even in the Green Zone near the US embassy.”

Analysts say the impending exit of US forces from Iraq comes amid key domestic challenges such as bringing all weapons under state control.

Prime Minister al-Zaidi this week reiterated a deadline for nonstate armed groups to disarm or face terrorism charges.

“The matter is linked to credibility and trust. Mr al-Zaidi was insistent and raised the ceiling of escalation regarding not backing down from the September 30 deadline to restrict weapons to the state,” al-Anbar said.

“We have now begun talking about ‘regulating’ weapons, and what is the mechanism of this regulation? No one talks about the details of this issue. We notice an escalation in the rhetoric of political parties like Kataib Sayyid al-Shuhada, Harakat al-Nujaba and Kataib Hezbollah.”

The question of how the government will manage the task of handling security alone amid such challenges remains a prominent one, particularly as key positions in the defence and interior ministries remain vacant.

“These ministries represent core points in the plan to begin restricting weapons to the state,” al-Anbar added.

The withdrawal of foreign soldiers from Iraq reflects a wider strategic shift by the US under President Donald Trump, rather than a complete disengagement from the country.

Former US diplomat Marlin Hardinger said Washington will remain engaged in security issues in Iraq despite the formal withdrawal.

“I think we can say this medium-term commitment has ended, and I believe there will be residual efforts related to counterterrorism and intelligence, especially around the US embassy as well as the consulate,” Hardinger told Al Jazeera.

“The Trump administration will perhaps focus more on the economic aspect and the developmental dimension so that the economic returns and benefits in the short and medium term are better for Iraqis, and then the position of the Iraqi prime minister will be stronger.”

The withdrawal will appeal to some Trump supporters, particularly among those in the America First contingent of the Republican Party. But it could also alarm some of Washington’s allies in the region, amid the ongoing US-Israel war on Iran.

“Factions supporting Israel that want direct US involvement in the Middle East may be displeased by this withdrawal; likewise, this could represent a danger to Gulf states if terrorist organisations emerge,” Hardinger said.

“The real problem is that the region has become less stable and more turbulent than it was when negotiations and discussions related to the withdrawal of American forces began.”

The withdrawal of US Patriot missile batteries could leave northern Iraq highly vulnerable to external threats, said Hassan al-Barari, an international relations professor at the University of Jordan.

“It is unlikely that the Iraqi state is currently capable of defending its skies against Iranian missiles and drones if Iran targets Erbil, for example [and] this raises a question at this stage about how to fill this security gap,” he told Al Jazeera.

“In the event Iran continues to send drones and missiles, who will intercept them if American Patriot systems and interceptor missiles withdraw? Who can stop this Iranian threat if there is no direct understanding with the government in Tehran?” al-Barari said.

Ultimately, the success of the transition depends entirely on Baghdad’s ability to manage domestic security issues.

“The ability of the Baghdad government to maintain or fully restore Iraq’s sovereignty is not only linked to the withdrawal of American forces, but also to al-Zaidi’s ability to restrict weapons to the state,” al-Barari said.

“In my view, things are heading towards the unknown. If al-Zaidi does not succeed in this, Iraq may fall completely under absolute Iranian influence … creating a dangerous security vacuum, which is the scenario Washington warns of and tries to avoid.”

articles.title: Detroit pastor says progressive candidates are trying to 'virtue-signal' to Christian voters
articles.summary: Detroit Pastor Lorenzo Sewell says progressive Senate candidates James Talarico, Angie Nixon and Abdul El-Sayed are using Jesus to win over voters.
articles.body: Detroit Pastor Lorenzo Sewell told Fox News Digital that progressive politicians are trying to "virtue-signal, placate, and try to propagate to Christians" because they represent the largest religious voting bloc in America. "It's the largest voting bloc in America. We're celebrating 250 years, where our forefathers — they understood that the God of the Bible, the Lord Jesus Christ, would give them the ability to start this great nation," Sewell said. "And we see that we've not been a perfect nation, but we understand that we've been the most benevolent." "We've been the nation that's protected Israel," he continued. "We've been the nation that, quite frankly, has spread Christianity throughout the world to reach hundreds of millions of people in the last 250 years." Three progressive Democratic candidates running for the U.S. Senate — Florida state Rep. Angie Nixon, former Michigan health official Abdul El-Sayed and Texas state Rep. James Talarico — shared a penchant for bucking the Democratic establishment in their high-profile primary bids this midterm cycle. They have also incorporated their religions and faiths into their campaigns and messaging to voters. JAMES TALARICO ADMITS PAST COMMENTS 'MISSED THE MARK' WHEN CONFRONTED ON CLAIMS LIKE GOD IS 'NON-BINARY' Talarico, a Texas state lawmaker and theological seminary graduate, has often cited biblical scripture to defend progressive policies, gaining national attention. Talarico has argued that Jesus focused on feeding the hungry, welcoming strangers, and helping the poor rather than engaging in partisan culture wars. "Imagine a Democratic Party that takes on big money and isn’t captured by it," Talarico told an audience of Democrats in Hays County, according to a report by the Texas Tribune. "Imagine a Democratic Party that delivers for people on housing, health care, and education, and actually defeats the right-wing extremists who have taken over this country." In a sermon laying out his progressive framing of the Bible, Talarico asked what Jesus would do "about a tax system that benefits the rich over the poor" and "a health care system that forces the sick to start GoFundMe pages to afford lifesaving surgeries." PROGRESSIVE FLORIDA LAWMAKER ANGIE NIXON TOPPLES TRUMP IMPEACHMENT WITNESS IN DEM SENATE PRIMARY UPSET During comments at the Saint Paul AME Church of Jacksonville, Florida, Nixon — the Democratic Senate nominee facing Republican incumbent Sen. Ashley Moody in November — contended that her political positions were akin to those of Jesus Christ. "They are trying, y'all. They are trying ... to label me as this extremist, this radical. But, you know, Jesus was a radical," Nixon said. El-Sayed, during an appearance on the "Progressive Christians Podcast" that aired in May, similarly invoked Christ when asked about his policy positions. El-Sayed, who is Muslim and running in Michigan's Senate race against former Republican Rep. Mike Rogers, was asked about the overlap between Islamic teachings and Christianity, and why his platform was being framed as radical. EL-SAYED MAKES JESUS COMPARISON WHEN PRESSED ON SOCIALIST VIEWS: 'RADICAL IN HIS TIME, TOO' "Well, you know, Jesus — peace and blessings be upon him — was considered radical in his time, too," El-Sayed said. Sewell insisted that progressive Democrats are simply playing politics with the electorate. "They know that they need to appeal to Christians. But the question becomes: What is their agenda for the church?" he said. "President Donald Trump has been the only president that has an agenda for the local church." "I was with them last week," Sewell added. "I'll be preaching at the RNC coming up, and that's because the president honors the church and honors the presence of God. But you won't hear Jesus in the DNC. You won't hear Jesus spoken about through the real Jesus — the God of the Bible." articles.title: West Bengal government bans liquor sales on Maha Ashtami, DJ music during Durga Puja
articles.summary: India News: NEW DELHI: West Bengal has announced a series of restrictions for this year’s Durga Puja, including a one-day ban on liquor sales, a complete prohibit.
articles.body: NEW DELHI: West Bengal has announced a series of restrictions for this year’s Durga Puja, including a one-day ban on liquor sales, a complete prohibition on DJ music and curbs on the use of major roads for Puja-related activities.Chief minister Suvendu Adhikari made the announcements on Monday at a coordination meeting with Durga Puja committees at Milan Mela Prangan. The measures are aimed at ensuring that celebrations remain peaceful and orderly.All liquor shops and bars across the state will remain closed on Maha Ashtami, when devotees offer anjali to Goddess Durga."On the day when devotees offer anjali (Maha Ashtami) to Maa Durga, all liquor shops in the state will remain closed. There will be no liquor available in bars either," he said.The decision comes despite liquor traditionally seeing strong demand during the Puja period.DJ music banned, themes to face scrutinyThe government will also prohibit DJ music during the celebrations and immersion processions.Adhikari asked Puja committees to ensure that their idols, pandals and themes do not offend religious sentiments or go against Sanatan traditions. Theme-based Pujas will still be allowed, but organisers have been asked to be more careful while choosing their concepts.The administration has also placed restrictions on roads being used for Puja activities. National highways cannot be blocked for organising Pujas, while 13 major roads in Kolkata, including Red Road and Cathedral Road, have been identified as areas where such activities will not be allowed.Puja inaugurations will also not be permitted before the start of Devi Paksha.Devi Paksha refers to the bright lunar fortnight in the Hindu month of Ashwin associated with the worship and invocation of Goddess Durga. The previous Trinamool Congress government under Mamata Banerjee had faced allegations over inaugurations being held before Devi Paksha began.Immersion deadline and special arrangementsAdhikari said organisers would have to complete idol immersions within the stipulated period before Lakshmi Puja."There will be no forcing or threatening anyone to change the immersion date," he said.The state has also planned cultural programmes in six major cities over two days, along with special events at six designated immersion ghats.Special arrangements will be made to help persons with disabilities, residents of old-age homes and people staying in ashrams visit Puja venues.The government will also set up an impartial jury for the Sharad Samman awards. Adhikari said the jury members would be chosen for their knowledge of the traditional, ritual and cultural aspects of Durga Puja. The Sharad Samman awards recognise Durga Puja organisers for creative and artistic excellence.The announcements come as West Bengal prepares for its first Durga Puja under the BJP government. The administration is seeking to manage the large-scale celebrations while imposing restrictions intended to maintain public order and protect religious and cultural sentiments.Get the latest India News and Live updates. articles.title: ‘Work day and night’: SC rejects Aravalli panel's extension plea; CJI says it's waiting for his retirement
articles.summary: India News: NEW DELHI: The Supreme Court on Monday refused to give the expert panel examining the definition and protection of the Aravalli Hills another six mont.
articles.body: NEW DELHI: The Supreme Court on Monday refused to give the expert panel examining the definition and protection of the Aravalli Hills another six months to submit its final report, telling it to "work day and night" and complete the exercise by November 30.A bench headed by Chief Justice Surya Kant and comprising Justices Joymalya Bagchi and V Mohana rejected the high-powered committee's request to extend the deadline till February 28, 2027. The court also warned that it would reconstitute the panel if it failed to submit the report within the next two months, news agency PTI reported."Let the panel work day and night to submit a report on the Aravalli issue. If they are unable to do that in two months, we will reconstitute the whole panel," the CJI observed.The court also directed the committee to submit issue-specific interim reports, allowing it to address urgent aspects of the contentious Aravalli definition without waiting for its comprehensive final report.The CJI appeared particularly unimpressed with the timing of the extension request, observing that the committee had sought more time "with the first stroke of the pen" and appeared to be waiting for his retirement.The court further directed the panel to hear all stakeholders, including tribal communities in Rajasthan and Gujarat, before finalising its recommendations. The matter will next be heard on December 2.The committee had sought six additional months, saying it needed more time to undertake a “comprehensive and defensible” assessment of the Aravalli range. Its deadline for submitting the final report was August 31.In its compliance report filed on August 31, the panel said its assessment required the integration of spatial, ecological, geological, hydrological and socio-economic evidence, besides inputs from stakeholders.It said additional time was needed for geospatial assessment, sensitivity analysis, expert examination, field verification and stakeholder validation.The committee also argued that the Aravalli issue could not be resolved through a “single terrain-based criterion or a single source of evidence”.The urgency around the exercise stems from a controversy over how the Aravallis should be defined for regulatory purposes, particularly mining.'Unfortunately & inexplicably': Congress reactsThe Congress expressed disappointment over the Supreme Court’s decision to reject the High Powered Committee’s request for a six-month extension to submit its final report on the Aravallis.Calling the decision “unfortunate and inexplicable”, party leader Jairam Ramesh said the committee’s request for an extension beyond August 31, 2026, was “most justifiable”. Congress maintained that the additional time was necessary for the committee to complete its work and submit a comprehensive report on the ecologically sensitive Aravalli range.Get the latest India News and Live updates.
